audit.note: Independent audit against quality-contract B. Repairs (one round): (1) accuracy: the freshness sentence let inclusion time and round numbers read as dating the observation; it now says these date the report rather than the observation, before the signer-timestamp caveat. (2) accuracy: the median now stays within the range of the correct (was: honest) reports while fewer than half are wrong, so the bound is about truth, which an honest but mistaken report does not carry. Accuracy otherwise checked: a TLS session alone yields no transferable evidence (symmetric session keys let the client forge a transcript), so web-data proof schemes commonly add a notary or proxy (TLSNotary, DECO, proxy-based zkTLS; TEE-based schemes are the exception, hence 'commonly' is right); trust in the TLS key, CAs and notary/proxy non-collusion is a fair compression. Enclave side-channel breaks 'more than once' holds (Foreshadow, SGAxe, Plundervolt, AEPIC Leak, Downfall). Median bound holds for odd and even n. Staking is stated conditionally (forfeiture depends on a false report being shown false by an accepted process); dispute windows conditionally (a watcher willing to challenge, an honest resolver), with the latency cost; redundancy as a condition on independence; all three 'bound the exposure without closing it'. No overclaim or inaccurate under-claim remains. Wording of the limit in the record: precise and conditional where it must be. The definition fixes the limit for reports of facts outside the protocol; paragraph 1 states it as 'for such a protocol [one that learns of the world only through reports] correspondence lies outside what checks on the report can establish'; the text never says 'never', and 'cannot settle by checking the report' is scoped. violatedBy case in the record: paragraph 2 frames a mistaken or compromised source signing a false value explicitly as 'not a breach of the limit but the case it leaves undetected', where the protocol's exposure lies; correct. Accepted model fields: statement's 'never its truth' is too strong unscoped and 'origin and form' omits freshness and agreement; suggested: 'checks on a report establish who signed it, that it is unaltered, how recent it is and how it agrees with other reports; for a protocol that learns of the world only through reports, they cannot establish that it is true of the world'. violatedBy is inaccurate for this concept: nothing a source does violates the limit; the case is the exposure the limit leaves. Suggested: drop violatedBy (statement, establishedBy and confusions still satisfy the property kind), or reword it as 'none; the exposure it leaves: a mistaken or compromised source signing a false value passes every check'. The record already follows the corrected reading, so it needs no change if the model is amended. Reservations: External Data is not delimited; 'a report of facts outside it' and 'a protocol that learns of the world only through reports' state the epistemic condition under which the limit holds, not what counts as external data. Trust Assumptions is not given a general account; 'taken on trust', 'relies on', 'trust moves to' and 'trust moves rather than disappears' name the specific reliance where each attestation form stops (owned claim 2), never what trust assumptions are or how they are stated for claims; the definition's 'what it has to accept without checking' identifies one thing accepted (truth), not the reserved notion. Authenticity is named ('authentic') and not explained; stating what a signature from a known key shows (which key, unaltered) and what source signing adds are owned claims (origin, integrity; signed data at the source), and the record avoids the key-to-source binding that authenticity owns. Siblings: oracle-failure is not pre-empted (no taxonomy of failure forms, causes or downstream effects; the mistaken/compromised source illustrates the limit's exposure only); external-data-availability is not touched (the dispute window's delay is latency of acceptance, not availability). Parent: extends the parent's single sentence on the limit into four checkable properties, the attestation forms and design-arounds; the stake incentive echoes the parent's corruption-cost margin but adds the mechanism and its dependence on proving falsity. Canonical: one leaf placement, no positional language, self-sufficient. Economy and progression: eight paragraphs, each carrying one step (checkable properties; why agreement falls short and the exposure; three attestation forms; three design-arounds); the summary sentence closing the web-data paragraph restates the three relocations but carries the conclusion that the step from statement to world stays, so it was kept. Prose decision matches the design.

resolutions.resolution: Economic Guarantees is named as one design-around (owned claim 3); the record says only what it does for an oracle report (stake forfeited if shown false, turning truth into incentive) and its dependence on a dispute process, not a general account of economic guarantees.
False match: 'trusted execution environment' contains the title of Execution Environments, a different concept (where autonomous agents run); it is neither named nor explained.
Oracle Nodes is named once as an intermediary that source signing removes from what is trusted; not explained.
Token Holders is named once as an example resolver ('a vote of token holders'); not explained.

Trusted Execution is named via 'trusted execution environment'; the record describes only what hardware attestation lets a protocol check and where it stops (owned claim 2), not how trusted execution works.
Zero-Knowledge is named once ('often a zero-knowledge one'); not explained.

Not unhedged: 'Economic guarantees' is a concept name; 'the guarantee depends on a false report being shown false' is explicitly conditional; 'a question the protocol cannot settle by checking the report' is scoped to checks on the report and holds under the stated condition.

audit.note: Audited against quality-contract section B under the single placement labelled "Data Availability". Three minimal repairs within the accepted claims and design. (1) Sibling and parent boundary: the oracle-failure sentence ended 'of which an absent value is one form', which listed one of oracle failure's own forms and repeated the parent's 'Oracle failure includes silence'; it is now a bare boundary naming oracle failure. (2) Accuracy: rate limits were 'caps ... or charges for each', but per-request charging does not by itself refuse requests; the clause now states only the cap. (3) Accuracy: rainfall at a field with no station was said to have 'no source at all', yet radar, satellite and interpolated gauge products estimate rainfall almost everywhere and parametric insurance uses them; it now says such a fact has no source of its own and estimates give a different figure, not the missing measurement. Judged acceptable: definition leads with the three conditions (source has the data, is reachable, keeps publishing); 'information from outside a chain' locates the data without delimiting what counts as external data, so the External Data reservation (facts a protocol cannot derive from its own state) is not explained or paraphrased; no text explains trust assumptions or authenticity. Accuracy holds: stock exchanges commonly close overnight, at weekends and on holidays; off-hours venues quote a different and often thinner market; deviation-triggered updates raise request demand in volatile markets; censorship by providers or authorities, discontinued feeds and delisting, and data not yet produced are stated correctly and under their conditions. Causes are availability causes (a source or its path, or absence in the world) and do not pre-empt oracle failure's causes (source errors, node faults, manipulation, delay) or its downstream effects. No overlap with verification-limits beyond the accuracy contrast, which is this concept's claim. Parent overlap: the parent says availability is part of the problem alongside accuracy; the record adds that either fails without the other and why checks of rightness cannot supply a missing value. Progression runs definition, identity distinction, demand and accuracy, source-side causes, world-side causes. Distinction: of value. The label 'Data Availability' is the title of the blockchain storage concept, and nothing in the prose mentions that concept, so the block is the only place the conflation is marked and it restates no prose. A bare two-label pair is the corpus's normal use (most of the ~300 distinction blocks have no further), and no third notion in the design would form a chain, so further is not warranted (accuracy is a separate prose claim, not a link in this chain). The definition's 'from outside a chain' with the paragraphs' sources, providers and markets gives the reader enough to tell the meanings apart without the record explaining data publication, withholding or sampling; the right label's own wording, together with the inspected data-availability record (committed data obtainable by participants), confirms it is accurate about that concept.

resolutions.resolution: data-availability appears only as the distinction's right label 'Blockchain data availability'; none of its mechanisms (publication, withholding, sampling, committees) is explained. Named, not explained, as the design requires.

external-data appears only inside this concept's own name and as 'information from outside a chain'; the text never states what counts as external data or paraphrases 'facts a protocol cannot derive from its own state'. Named, not explained.
'A lending market that values collateral' is an example of a demand pattern (current price at short intervals); lending markets are not explained. Named, not explained.

oracle-failure is named once as a boundary: 'What a missing value then does to a protocol is a matter of oracle failure.' After repair it no longer lists oracle failure's forms, causes or effects. Named, not explained.

audit.note: Independent audit against quality contract section B, read at the single placement (Oracles & External Reality / Oracle Problem / Oracle Failure, leaf). Failure-kind modelling: sound and followed. The definition states a condition (no correct value in time for a dependent decision), not an act; paragraph 1 works through causes (source errors, faulty or offline nodes, delay) and places deliberate manipulation explicitly as one cause among several that yields the same forms, naming oracle manipulation without explaining it; paragraph 2 and the comparison give manifestation; paragraphs 3-4 give impact; detection and recovery are named only. Comparison: earns its place. Reading across the four forms on what the protocol sees, typical cause and consequence shows what prose would spread over several sentences (only the wrong value is fresh and false; only the late value is right; stale and missing differ in what reaches the protocol, not in their cause). Cells are accurate and the rows distinct: stale (an old value persists and reads as current, no replacement coming) versus late (a correct update exists but misses the decision, so the harm is bounded to the gap) is a real difference as written. The stale and missing cause cells overlap in substance, which is consistent with paragraph 2's point that read design (push keeps the last value, pull needing a fresh report gets nothing) decides which form a halt takes; acceptable. 'A source with nothing to give' names the category Data Availability explains without explaining it; acceptable. The prose does not spell out cells: paragraph 3 explains propagation (speed of liquidators, liquidations standing once confirmed, bad debt from overvalued collateral, unrecoverable settlement, the late-value trading window, slow losses while frozen), which is the design's division. Repairs: (1) Territory/recovery by paraphrase: the closing sentences explained a consumer-side guard that rejects values by the size of the move and its false-trip cost (freezing a market during a real crash); that is the deviation-measuring breaker and its missed-incident versus false-trip trade-off, owned by Circuit Breakers, and it echoed the parent's 'each response chooses which failure the protocol would rather suffer'. Removed; the frozen-market impact remains covered by the comparison and paragraph 3. (2) Accuracy: 'Staleness checks and heartbeats exist to detect such failures' overclaimed (they do not detect erratic prices; heartbeats bound update intervals rather than detect); now 'exist to expose updates that are late or have stopped', with recovery mechanisms 'to contain the damage'. (3) Accuracy: a source error 'is diluted' implied averaging; median aggregation excludes rather than dilutes, so now 'contained'. Accepted findings: the source-error sentence (adding nodes that read one source does not contain its error) sits close to Verification Limits' independence condition on redundancy, but it answers this concept's own question, how far a cause travels to become a wrong value, and does not explain redundancy as a design; acceptable. Accuracy checks passed: congestion coinciding with sharp price moves (hedged 'most likely'); push versus pull behaviour on a halt; liquidations standing once confirmed; settlement not recovered by correcting the record. Parent overlap: none beyond expanding 'silence as well as falsehood' into four forms. Siblings and reservations (External Information, Trust Assumptions, Data Authenticity, Data Availability, Verification Limits) are not explained. No positional language; economy and progression (definition, causes, form, comparison, consequences, correlation) good.

resolutions.resolution: Circuit breakers are named once, in a list of containment means; after repair no sentence explains how a breaker or guard trips or its false-trip trade-off. Named, not explained.
Heartbeats (excluded) are named once with a one-word role (expose late or stopped updates); no interval, trigger or check is explained. Named, not explained.
'Lending market' is the setting of an impact example; only the liquidation behaviour the impact needs is described, not how lending markets work. Named, not explained.
Oracle manipulation (excluded) is named as the subject that covers how manipulation is carried out; the text only classifies manipulation as one cause yielding the same forms. Named, not explained.

Staleness (excluded) appears as 'staleness checks' named with a role and as the stale-value form, which is this concept's own claim (a form of failure), not the freshness mechanism or its thresholds. Named, not explained.

groupAudit.note: Read side by side with the parent. Reservations: no member, nor the three together, defines or delimits External Data, Trust Assumptions or Authenticity. External Data is only named (VL 'a report of facts outside it', EDA 'information from outside a chain', OF not at all); none says what counts as external. Trust Assumptions is the closest approach: VL's definition ('what it has to accept without checking') echoes the reservation wording, and its attestation paragraphs say what trust moves to for each form (provider and its key, chip vendor, TLS key, certificate authorities and notary). That is VL's claim 2 ('where each stops') applied to named mechanisms; nothing states what a trust assumption is or how to state one, so it stays application, not definition. Authenticity is covered only through VL's claim-1 origin and integrity sentence ('a valid signature from a known key shows which key signed the report and that its content has not changed since') and the source-signing paragraph, both framed as where the check stops; EDA and OF do not touch it. Naming is consistent: 'authentic' once in VL, 'trust' as verb or noun, never a redefinition. Overlap: VL vs OF on correlated sources is the thickest. The fact that sources sharing an upstream feed defeat redundancy appears in VL para 3 (agreement), VL's redundancy paragraph (independence) and OF para 2 (a source error reaches every node that reads it). Each angle belongs to its own concept (agreement is not truth; redundancy depends on independence; where a fault enters decides how far it travels), so this is tolerable, not a defect. The median statements are consistent: VL's 'stays within the range of the correct reports as long as fewer than half are wrong' fits OF's 'contained only where the aggregate also draws on sources that do not share the error'. EDA vs OF: there is a clean hand-off. EDA gives the upstream causes and ends 'What a missing value then does to a protocol is a matter of oracle failure'. OF gives the forms and cites 'a halted source' and 'a source with nothing to give' only as causes. So a missing value is consistently a failure form whose cause can be an availability matter, with no contradiction. Staleness and freshness are treated once each: VL covers what a freshness check dates (the report, not the observation), OF names stale and late values as forms, and staleness checks and heartbeats are named only, as excluded. EDA does not treat staleness. Timestamps, inclusion time and on-chain inclusion delay are consistent across VL and OF. Terms: report (VL), value (all), source and provider (EDA, VL) and node/reporter (OF/VL) are used coherently. VL's 'reporters' generalizes nodes to include proposers in stake and dispute schemes. Minor defects for the human reviewer, none blocking: (1) OF uses 'feed' in two senses. In 'a feed mapped to the wrong asset', listed as an error at a source, it means an input feed, and that example is ambiguous because a mis-mapped oracle feed is an integration fault, not a source error. In 'becomes a failure of the feed when too few do' and 'until the feed resumes' it means the oracle's output. VL and EDA use 'feed' only for an upstream or provider feed. Proposed fix in OF para 2: replace 'or a feed mapped to the wrong asset' with 'or a quote mapped to the wrong asset', and 'becomes a failure of the feed when too few do' with 'becomes a failure of the oracle when too few do'. (2) EDA's definition frames external data as 'information from outside a chain', while the parent and VL frame it as outside the protocol's own state. Data from another chain is external to a protocol but not 'outside a chain'. Proposed fix: 'the information from outside its own chain that a protocol depends on'. Alternatively, if the contrast with blockchain data availability is wanted, keep the chain framing, since it stays a naming of the reserved External Data either way. (3) OF's comparison splits one cause across two rows: 'a halted source' under Stale value and 'a source with nothing to give' under Missing value. OF's own para 3 says that the same halt appears as stale or missing depending on how the protocol reads. The cells are hedged as 'Typical cause', so this does not contradict the paragraph; optionally align the Missing value cause to 'Too few working nodes, or a halted source read on demand'. Repetition: the openings are definitional as required and differ in shape ('are the boundary between', 'is whether', 'is a condition in which'), and the second paragraphs open differently. Forms differ per concept: VL is prose only (8 paragraphs), EDA has a distinction and 3 paragraphs, OF has 4 paragraphs and a comparison. There is no cloned structure. EDA's distinction marks a real conflation, given its contextual label 'Data Availability'. One phrase echo: EDA 'another source that does not share them can still have the data' and OF 'sources that do not share the error' make the same containment move with the same wording. It is acceptable, but a reviewer may vary one. Spelling: the corpus convention is American (-ize, behavior, defense); the only variant-bearing word in the group is OF 'organized', which is consistent, and there are no British forms. Plan weakness: VL's claims 1 and 2 (origin and integrity; signed data at the source) cover in substance what the Authenticity reservation names ('unaltered from its claimed source'). The boundary rests on angle (where the check stops) rather than content, so a later Authenticity author must relate to VL rather than restate it. No group signals were raised.
